when making the first project i was excited to figure out workflows that will continue for the rest of the project (specifically the mundane task of organizing collections).

i think there was struggle with coming to terms that this project is going to take longer than i thought. in the past i have cramped projects to fit in a deadline that was previously outlined for me. while i still have to adhere to that, this really can go beyond the semester.

i feel at an in-between (lol) myself and i would love to do more fun "activations" like wheat pasting or artist objects inspired from this collection but i am struggling with what to do. i like eric's idea of mounting on a wood panel and photographing it in front of their locations. i would like if someone could help me brainstorm more ideas for these things.

i'm nervous but am thinking about are.na api a lot. i haven't coded in so long that i'm in a bit of disbelief that i took 2 coding courses and can't remember a single thing about the subject i got to brush up on this. i'll have to schedule another meeting with aaryan again. it's insane that no one tells you HOW to plug an api into your code. there's tutorials for everything else but this. are.na how do you have a developers section with no basic page that tells me what pages i need and where to copy and paste stuff. ack! these things are my fault mostly.

once i get someone's selection of cards for the book i will make a book template for me to rinse and repeat this publication series.

i should wheat paste again.......... i really should.......... i might need to make the dimensions a bit smaller for it to be a smoother process but that's ok

i also have to stop thinking things are corny before i actually do it. i loooove a conceptual project but will hesitate a lot in advance. we chatted about playing in the fantasy which i am not opposed to but i gotta figure that out. we'll see. not so sure. never am!
